title: **Await lowering relaxes declaration semantics** — in transformed programs, top-level `let`, `const`, and `class` bindings are mutable and initialized to `undefined` before execution; the native temporal dead zone does not apply. Function d...

attrs.text: **Await lowering relaxes declaration semantics** — in transformed programs, top-level `let`, `const`, and `class` bindings are mutable and initialized to `undefined` before execution; the native temporal dead zone does not apply. Function declarations populate retained globals when execution reaches them, and a `var` declaration without an initializer resets its binding to `undefined`. Direct-eval declarations stay within that evaluation. Top-level `using` declarations are rejected; put disposable bindings inside a block. Runtime stack locations refer to the transformed source. Scripts that compile without lowering keep native semantics.

title: **Failed native lexical initialization can reserve a name** — if a top-level `let`, `const`, or `class` initializer throws before initializing its binding, that name remains uninitialized in the retained Script context. Reading, assigning o...

attrs.text: **Failed native lexical initialization can reserve a name** — if a top-level `let`, `const`, or `class` initializer throws before initializing its binding, that name remains uninitialized in the retained Script context. Reading, assigning or redeclaring it fails; use a new name or release and recreate the environment.

title: **Scoped REPL copies values when a call starts** — with `replScoped` omitted or `true`, assignments that earlier code makes afterwards stay invisible to later calls, and a `let`, `const` or `class` redeclaration cannot read the earlier valu...

attrs.text: **Scoped REPL copies values when a call starts** — with `replScoped` omitted or `true`, assignments that earlier code makes afterwards stay invisible to later calls, and a `let`, `const` or `class` redeclaration cannot read the earlier value of its own name. A `var` redeclaration starts from that value, so `var count = count + 1` adds to it, also after an earlier `let` or `const` of the same name. Relative `import()` specifiers keep resolving from the environment's first working directory after a later call changes directory; relative file access follows the current directory. The `codeGeneration` limit rejects only the program context's own `eval`, `Function` and WebAssembly compilation and is no isolation: main-realm functions copied into the context, such as `setTimeout.constructor`, still compile code. Columns after the inserted completion on the final expression's line shift right by 17, programs that start with `#!` or contain `__$binding_` anywhere are rejected, binding-global and error-class names containing that prefix fail before process launch, and a surviving function keeps every value copied into its call. The [scoped REPL decision](../../../.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-11-09-retained-ptc-scoped-repl.md) lists the complete behavior.
